Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel for the 
petitioners.
2. Mr. N.S. Pundir, learned Dy.AG, for the 
State of Uttarakhand/1 to 3.
3. By the instant petition, the petitioners are 
praying for the following reliefs:-
“A. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of 
certiorari for quashing the order dated 16th of May 
2014 passed by the respondent No.3, whereby, 
alleging continuous absence of Late Ram Chandra 
Singh who was the husband and father respectively 
of the petitioners, the services on the post of 
Chowkidar have been terminated. (Annexure No.10 
to this writ petition) 
B. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of 
mandamus directing the respondents to sanction the 
family pension of the petitioner no.1 and further to 
pay all arrears of pension accrued from the date it 
becomes due till date it is paid alongwith the interest 
at the rate of 18% per annum.
C. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of 
mandamus directing the respondents to consider the 
case of the petitioner No.2 for the grant of 
compassionate appointment on a suitable post, 
inasmuch as, all other petitioners has already given 
NOC for the same.
D. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of 
mandamus directing the respondents to grant and 
release the salary of deceased Ram Chandra Singh to 
the petitioners from 6th of December 2006 till the 
date of civil death i.e. 07.02.2015 or actual death i.e. 
16.09.2020 and further all post retiral cum death 
benefits be granted and paid to the petitioners.”
4. The petitioner no.1 is the wife of the  deceased employee – Late Ram Chandra Singh,
who was serving in a Class IV post as a Peon in 
Public Works Department, and all the remaining 
petitioners are the sons and unmarried daughters, 
and as apprise none of the family members are in 
any job. In the year 2012, it has been noted by the 
Department that the deceased employee was not 
mentally fit, and is absent from the office also, and 
therefore, the family members may be informed 
about his mental condition.
5. Subsequently by an office order dated 
16.05.2014, the services of the deceased employee 
was terminated on the ground of long absence 
from duties without holding the disciplinary 
proceeding. Thereafter in the year 2015, the 
concerned Civil Court declared the deceased 
employee to be dead. Subsequently in the year of
2020, a dead body was recovered which was 
identified of deceased employee. 
6. By the instant petition, the termination order 
of the deceased employee is being challenged on 
the ground that without holding a disciplinary 
proceeding the order of termination was passed 
and is bad in law and cannot sustain and secondly 
the deceased employee was disabled and was not 
medically fit, consequently, therefore the 
Department was under legal obligation to proceed 
in terms of Section 47 of the Persons with 
Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of 
Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995, which 
read as under:-
“47. Non-discrimination in Government employment 
.- (1) No establishment shall dispense with, or reduce in 
rank, an employee who acquires a disability during his 
service:
Provided that, if an employee, after acquiring disability is not 
suitable for the post he was holding, could be shifted to some 
other post with the same pay scale and service benefits:
Provided further that if it is not possible to adjust the employee 
against any post, he may be kept on a supernumerary post 
until a suitable post is available or he attains the age of 
superannuation, whichever is earlier. (2) No promotion shall be denied to a person merely on 
the ground of his disability:
Provided that the appropriate Government may, having regard 
to the type of work carried on in any establishment, by 
notification and subject to such conditions, if any, as may be 
specified in such notification, exempt any establishment from 
the provisions of this section.”
7. On perusal of the aforesaid provision and 
the fact that without holding the disciplinary 
proceedings the order of termination was passed, 
therefore, apparently the termination order is bad 
in law and since the instant petition is preferred 
under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, 
therefore, the laches in challenging the order of 
termination of the deceased employee will not 
come into the way. 
8. So far as the other reliefs are concerned, the
same are consequential one, however, this Court is 
primarily of the view that the order of termination 
of the deceased employee is bad and is illegal. 
9. Learned DAG for the State seeks time to get 
the detail instructions or to file a response. Let the 
response be filed positively on or before 
31.10.2026.
10. Put up this matter on 02.11.2026.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 14.10.2026
Nitesh/
